head-of-market-research.rationale: Both responses catch all twelve planted issues, make no arithmetic or external-import errors, and reach the same well-gated DEFER verdict. B handles the focus item K4 better: it quantifies the 55%/78% range from the memo's own inputs and gives a named specialist the job of reconciling the three views. It also adds integrative points that A lacks, such as sizing the lagoon claim and questioning the utility baseline.

investment-banking.rationale: Both responses find all twelve planted issues, handle the four focus items (K1, K2, K9, K10) correctly, cite memo lines, and reject the L28 Goldman benchmark. A wins narrowly because every number in it is correct, while B misstates the occupancy sensitivity as '±20%'; B's slightly richer gating does not outweigh an arithmetic slip in an investment-banking review built on numbers.

project-technology.rationale: Both responses find all twelve planted issues with correct arithmetic and handle the focus items well. B states its confidence more precisely, sets explicit constraints (peak-day capacity, a no-technology base case, an unsupported utility baseline) and has no factual slips about the memo, while A claims HIGH confidence throughout and mixes up stabilised adviser forecasts with year-1 occupancy.

syndications.rationale: Both responses catch all twelve planted issues, keep the Goldman Sachs benchmark out of their figures, withhold NPV/IRR/DSCR and set out a staged recourse-then-refinance capital path. B goes further: it calculates the 55% and 78% adviser cases without averaging them, notes where the double count might only be partial, separates high confidence on 'not financeable' from low confidence on 'fixable', and gives explicit lender thresholds. A also contains a stray 'Aquaverse' reference from outside the memo.

real-estate-hospitality.rationale: Both responses are accurate and traceable, pass every must-pass check, and correctly recalculate K1 and preserve the K4 adviser range rather than averaging it. B is slightly more useful for a decision: it gives a nuanced NO-GO-as-proposed verdict, explicitly withholds NPV and total revenue, spots the hotel-guest overlap with the tourist total, and assigns more concrete per-specialist tasks and gates, while A's only edge is explicitly labelling the L32 sponsor conclusion.

ai-strategy.rationale: Both responses handle the focus items K6 and K5 correctly, withhold NPV/IRR/DSCR and reject the Goldman Sachs benchmark. A goes further on payment-agent controls and the utility arithmetic. B is preferred narrowly because it covers all twelve planted issues, including the schedule (K12) and the conference revenue left out of the revenue build, while A misses K12; B's one slip, calling the 23-point adviser spread '15 points', does not change any conclusion.

environmental-technologies.rationale: Both responses find almost the same issues, label sponsor claims and reject the Goldman benchmark, but B gets the sequential-savings arithmetic wrong on its own focus item (USD 0.265m instead of 0.530m remaining), while A's overlap arithmetic and reasoning are correct. A also keeps the adviser disagreement open and tests both ends, and it makes the stronger point that a new build cannot have a 'current' baseline bill.
